title: Minimum Moves to Reach Target Score
summary: Starting with the integer 1, you aim to reach the target integer using a limited number of doubling operations.
statement: Starting with the integer 1, you aim to reach the target integer using a limited number of doubling operations. You are allowed to increment the current integer by one or double it, but you can only perform the doubling operation up to maxDoubles times. The objective is to determine the minimum number of moves needed to reach the target.
constraints: Start at score one; each move increments by one or doubles, with at most max_doubles doublings.
Scores never need to exceed target.
Return the minimum moves to reach target.
hints: Reverse the process: decrement odd targets and halve even targets while doublings remain.
A reverse halving replaces the only useful final doubling; an odd target must first lose one increment.
Loop while target>1 and doubles remain, then add target-1 remaining decrements.
Each greedy reverse step is forced or dominates repeated decrements, and after doublings run out only unit moves remain.
editorial: Each greedy reverse step is forced or dominates repeated decrements, and after doublings run out only unit moves remain.

tests.explanation: Without doubling, four increments move from one to five.
Working backward uses two halvings and the necessary decrements for seven moves.
